content: The patient is a 77-year-old male with a significant past medical history that includes hypertension (HTN), benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), coronary artery disease (CAD) with coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), myocardial infarction (MI), and aortic valve replacement (AVR). His past surgical history includes: Aortic valve replacement (AVR) with a 25 Magna Ease valve performed on December 14, 2017. Coronary artery stent placement on October 10, 2017. Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in 2007. Appendectomy in 1957. The patient is currently on the following medications: Metoprolol Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) Tamsulosin On December 26, 2017, the patient presented with symptoms of right leg collapse, as well as weakness in the right arm and right leg. These episodes lasted approximately 2 to 10 minutes and occurred 1 to 4 times per day. The patient did not report any visual or speech difficulties, headache, or neck pain. There was no history of vertigo, syncope, loss of consciousness, or seizures. A physical examination revealed a normal neurological exam, with a blood pressure of 124/66 mmHg and a heart rate of 96 beats per minute. Imaging and diagnostic studies included: MRI of the brain on January 3, 2018, which showed no evidence of vascular occlusion or restricted diffusion to suggest infarction. MRA of the head and neck on the same date, which revealed an eccentric filling defect in the left internal carotid artery just distal to the bifurcation, possibly due to calcification or a non-occlusive thrombus. Carotid ultrasound (preliminary) on January 3, 2018, which showed 1-49% stenosis of both the right and left internal carotid arteries. Bilateral vertebral arteries were patent with antegrade flow. EEG on January 3, 2018, which was normal, with no epileptiform discharges, focal changes, or other abnormalities. A neurology consultation was conducted on January 3, 2018, with the following recommendations: Complete blood count (CBC) and comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP). Admission to the neurology service. MRI of the brain with or without contrast. MRA of the extracranial and intracranial circulation. Carotid duplex ultrasound. EEG. The suggested treatments included: Aspirin 81 mg chewable tablet. Clopidogrel 75 mg tablet. Enoxaparin 40 mg injection. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg extended-release tablet. The clinical course and patient condition were monitored, with documentation of whether the patient’s condition improved or worsened over time.
